title: Find All K-Distant Indices in an Array
summary: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums and integers key and k, identify all indices i where there exists at least one index j such that the absolute difference between i and j is less than or equal to k and nums[j] equals key.
statement: Given a 0-indexed integer array nums and integers key and k, identify all indices i where there exists at least one index j such that the absolute difference between i and j is less than or equal to k and nums[j] equals key. Return these indices in ascending order.
constraints: An index qualifies if some key occurrence lies within absolute distance k.
Return each qualifying index exactly once in increasing order.
k may be zero, in which case only key positions qualify.
hints: Each key occurrence contributes an inclusive interval of qualifying indices.
Use a difference array to add all intervals, then scan their union once.
Increment at max(0,j-k), decrement after min(n-1,j+k), prefix-sum, and emit positions with positive coverage.
Difference updates represent every neighborhood exactly, and positive prefix coverage is equivalent to existence of at least one qualifying key index.
editorial: Difference updates represent every neighborhood exactly, and positive prefix coverage is equivalent to existence of at least one qualifying key index.

tests.explanation: The two key positions cover index intervals [1,3] and [4,6], whose union is 1 through 6.
Every position is itself or is near a key, so all indices are returned once.
